findings.item: H1 says what the page is about
findings.detail: only 12 characters; none of the brief's words appear in it
findings.fix: An H1 should name the service and the place: “Testimonials” reads as a slogan, not a subject.
A jump from H2 to H4 reads to a crawler as a missing section. Demote or promote so each level follows the one above.
Service, then place, then brand: “Aesthetic Clinic in Johor Bahru | Klinik Suzana”. Set it in Yoast on import.

findings.item: Enough on the page to rank

findings.detail: the first screen mentions 1 of the brief's words
findings.fix: Say what the business is and where, in the first paragraph, in the words people search for.

findings.detail: 267 blocks are still the template's words
findings.fix: Template copy describes a different business. It is the single biggest thing holding this page back, ranking and conversion both.
“Read more” tells a crawler nothing about what it points at. Name the destination: “See our skin treatments”.

findings.item: Internal links to the rest of the site

findings.fix: Alt text is the only thing a crawler reads of a photo. Describe it plainly; do not list keywords.

findings.detail: 31 image(s) are named after a hash
findings.fix: Rename them before upload: “skin-clinic-johor-bahru-treatment-room.jpg”. It is most of image search.

findings.detail: no canonical link on the page
findings.fix: Set it in Yoast once the page has a real URL. It is what stops a duplicate at ?utm= splitting the page's own signals.

items: How Sitemark broke through an $18M plateau and grew 47% in six months.

findings.item: Name, address and phone all on the page
findings.detail: missing from the page: address, phone
findings.fix: A model deciding whether two mentions are the same business matches on these three together. One missing and the page stops confirming the entity.
